metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my friend's cafe called Brew Lab in Bengaluru, with the menu, timings, where it is, a photo gallery and some stories about where their coffee comes from

review.verdict: Clean one-cycle build: all 10 done-when items passed on 65 of 80 budget with no redirects, conflicts or rework, but the brief was too easy to test negotiation, conflict handling or lessons.

identity.note: Asked the needed questions in one round [2] and closed with a plain done message [35]. Slips: [5] is addressed to @Adaptation but written to the Requester, and [35] omits Audit's low warning [34].

adaptation.note: One proposal covered all 10 done-when items and kept 15 in reserve for one fix [7]. It never faced a counter, so revision behaviour is untested. The proposal fields are not visible in the chat.

priority.note: Granted all seven with reserve math [8]. 'Run styling last' [8] steps into Coordination's ordering job. The seven later envelope checks [11-30] add no new decision. Turns (27) exceed AI calls (20), so those checks may be code-generated (inferred, unverified).

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule each time and kept one writer, with no collisions. Both W-7 HOLDs [22][26] covered a workflow it had already ordered last [10], and caused a 5 release and recharge [23][30]. Accurate, but low value.

audit.note: Checked all 10 items and raised a useful risk: overflow-x: clip could hide overflow from the scrollWidth check [34]. It did not comment on the 'warm look' standard. The clip claim cannot be verified from the chat.

W-1.note: Honest that the nav targets did not exist yet [12].

W-3.note: Open 8am to 10pm every day, no closed day [18].

W-4.note: Correct address and tap-to-call link, no invented links [21].

W-5.note: Six labelled empty spots, no img elements [25]. The number six was the builder's choice, not a Requester fact.

W-6.note: Three stories using only supplied facts [28]. Audit found no invented facts [34].

W-7.note: Honest that overflow was unverified [31]. But its report lists a viewport tag, a reset and a footer, not warm styling or width rules. The footer was outside its declared scope. Whether the look is warm was never checked.

went_well: Declared dependencies plus one write lock: 7 sections, 7 site versions, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 failed workflows.
One question round [2] got every fact [4]. The charter has nothing to be confirmed and no invented contacts.
Hold accounting works: budget fell 65 to 60 on the hold [23] and returned to 65 when W-7 ran [30].
The code render check [33] and Audit [34] agree on no overflow, no JS errors and no broken links.
problems: The run exercised no hard path: 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts, 0 validator refusals, no lessons saved.
The rate card makes estimate equal charged for all seven workflows (10=10, 5=5), so Adaptation's estimating is not measured.
Item 9 warning stayed open [34]. If clip hides overflow, the code check [33] could pass falsely (unverified).
'Warm, simple look' is a charter standard but not a done-when item, so nothing tested it.
Overhead: 27 turns for an 11.6 KB page, 15 of them Priority and Coordination.
learnings: Keep the single write lock with declared dependencies. Evidence: zero collisions and zero invalid moves, though only on a simple page.
Change the render check to compare element right edges with viewport width, or flag overflow-x clip/hidden. Evidence: [33] and [34].
Test next: the same brief with a budget near 40 and one fact the Requester lacks. That forces COUNTER or REFUSE, a to-be-confirmed item and a lesson, none of which this run reached.
Run once with the rate card off, or drop estimate_vs_charged. As it stands it cannot show estimating skill.
Put the look standard into done-when with a checkable proxy (colour variables, a media query), or accept it goes unaudited.

Compare a 3-workflow split with the 7-workflow split on the same brief for calls and cost. The trade-off is less per-section ownership. Check the call log first to see whether Priority's per-run checks cost AI calls.
